solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chief cad? Absolutely

definitions.meaning: a chief is a HEAD and cads are HEELS, so the head is placed over the heels
absolutely = completely, utterly, as when falling for someone

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic reading: a chief is a HEAD, cads are HEELS, so the chief of cads is the head placed over the heels. The question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Head over heels means completely or utterly, as in head over heels in love, so it can stand for absolutely.

clue.text: New assembly of cruel and humane characters preserved city

indicators.note: a new assembly of the letters means putting them together in a different order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters: the characters (letters) of cruel and humane

explanation.surface: A parliament of mixed temperaments gathers to run a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' is the hint that cruel and humane are to be read as letters rather than qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculaneum was the Roman town buried and preserved by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79, alongside Pompeii.

clue.text: Put on suit

definitions.meaning: put on as with paint or cream spread onto a surface

definitions.note: suit as a verb meaning to petition or make a request, which is what applying is
definitions.meaning: suit as a verb: to petition or make a formal request

explanation.walkthrough: You apply paint or cream when you put it on, and to apply for something is to make a suit, an old word for a formal request.
explanation.definitionFit: Apply means put on (a layer, a bandage) and also means to make a formal request, the sense of suit in a suitor's plea.

clue.text: Planning nothing contrary during trip

parts.note: a trip or excursion is an outing

indicators.note: going contrary means running the opposite way

parts.note: nil = nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a journey without any plan at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' sounds like an attitude to the trip; it is the instruction to turn nothing round.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlining a scheme is sketching its main points, which is planning it.

clue.text: Key stage before final reversion of property

parts.note: the Escape key on a computer keyboard is marked ESC
a heat is a qualifying round, a stage run before the final

explanation.surface: Some keystroke in a process comes just before the last one, then property changes hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before final' belongs with 'stage', describing a heat; it is not an instruction to put ESC first.
explanation.definitionFit: Escheat is the legal reversion of property to the state or a lord when the owner dies without heirs.

clue.text: Bands for securing horse that went astray

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
'oops' is what you say when something goes astray

explanation.surface: Straps are used to tie up a horse that had wandered off.
explanation.walkthrough: The horse is not an animal here: H for heroin is a standard crossword abbreviation, and OOPS is the exclamation for a mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoops are the metal bands that hold a barrel's staves together.

clue.text: Rudimentary XI's first half unbalanced

indicators.note: keeping the first half of ELEVEN means taking its first three letters

parts.note: XI is ELEVEN in Roman numerals; its first half is ELE
mental = unbalanced, mad

explanation.surface: A cricket or football eleven plays crudely and loses its head in the first half.
explanation.walkthrough: XI looks like a team sheet, and a side of eleven is the picture; you need the word ELEVEN, spelt out, and then only half of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means basic or rudimentary, to do with first principles.

clue.text: The woman at the heart of British Empire

indicators.note: the answer sits right in the middle of the phrase British Empire

parts.note: britiSH Empire: the middle three of its thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A woman, perhaps Victoria or Britannia, stands at the centre of the Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart here is exact: S, H, E are the three central letters of BRITISHEMPIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain pronoun substitution: the woman, already mentioned, is referred to in the third person feminine.

clue.text: Make a slow escape, taking irrational road westward

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A fugitive creeps away slowly, choosing a mad route heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' reads as an adjective about the road; it is the noun for PI, an irrational number.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid that drips escapes slowly, a drop at a time.

clue.text: Cab's recording device disabled remote chat

indicators.note: a disabled machine is broken, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A taxi's radio link to its dispatcher has been switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: A cab here is a lorry or vehicle cab, not only a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A tachometer records engine or vehicle speed, the kind of instrument fitted in a vehicle's cab.

clue.text: Where one might put in vocally critical team?

indicators.note: vocally means said out loud, so we want what the phrase sounds like

parts.note: critical = key, team = side; say KEY SIDE and spell it the harbour way

explanation.surface: A spectator shouts to put a harsh opponent in their place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in' is the sailing sense: a ship puts in at a port. Quay is pronounced 'key'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quayside is the edge of a harbour where a vessel puts in to moor.

clue.text: Mug grasps end of clasp that doesn't need fastening

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for an adjective describing a garment

parts.note: a stein is a large beer mug

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of clasP

explanation.surface: A cup holds the tip of a buckle that never needed doing up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase 'that doesn't need fastening', describing a garment you simply step into.
explanation.definitionFit: Step-in clothes or shoes are ones you simply step into, with no buttons or laces to fasten.

clue.text: Heads of Church Union in Lourdes treated like sceptics

indicators.note: the letters are treated, processed into a new form
the heads of words are their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of Church and Union
anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Church leaders at the healing shrine of Lourdes are handled as if they were doubters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it should put CU inside something, but it is simply two more letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sceptics are incredulous: unwilling to believe what they are told.

clue.text: Overweight boxer getting endless abuse resigned

indicators.note: with no end, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: fat = overweight
Muhammad Ali, the boxer
STICK (abuse, as in taking stick) without its last letter

explanation.surface: A heavy boxer, abused without end, finally gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: Stick is British slang for criticism or abuse, as in 'to take stick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatalistic person is resigned, accepting whatever happens as inevitable.

clue.text: Fun goddess the author's appended to a religious text

indicators.note: appended means added on, so the pieces are joined end to end

parts.note: the article as printed
the Muses were goddesses of the arts
the author of the clue refers to themself as ME
NT = New Testament

explanation.surface: A writer attaches a playful goddess to some scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'the author's appended' as 'the author is appended': the clue's writer is added after the goddess, and the pair then follows 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fun and amusement both mean enjoyment or entertainment.

clue.text: Collected material perverted man copied

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A deviant has been photocopying a collection of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perverted' reads as describing the man, but it is the instruction to rearrange MAN COPIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Compendia, plural of compendium, are collections of material gathered into one work.

clue.text: Second sign of approval that may torment pet

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in the sound a clock makes each second
a blood-sucking parasite of dogs and cats

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions in a row: a tick is a moment (the clock's tick), a check mark, and a blood-sucking parasite.
explanation.definitionFit: Tick means a second (just a tick), a mark of approval, and a parasite that bothers dogs and cats.

clue.text: Lover's knot you might catch?

indicators.note: catching words means hearing them, so we want a sound

parts.note: a looped knot in a ribbon, the kind that rhymes with 'go'

explanation.surface: A romantic partner ties a love knot that you might just catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow rhymes with 'go' here, the knot in a ribbon, and beau is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A slightly old-fashioned synonym, borrowed from French, for a woman's boyfriend or admirer.

clue.text: Swimmer's haircut an ageing nonconformist might sport?

definitions.meaning: any creature that swims, here a fish

definitions.text: haircut an ageing nonconformist might sport?
definitions.meaning: a mullet is a haircut favoured by rebels, grey once they age

explanation.surface: A swimmer's hair is cut in the style of an old rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: a mullet is the short-front, long-back hairstyle, and an ageing rebel's would be grey.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this coastal fish is one kind of swimmer, while the second reading describes a hairstyle.

clue.text: England's opening pair, gutted, played again

indicators.note: the opening pair of a word is its first two letters

parts.note: the first two letters of ENgland
an apple cored has had its insides taken out

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen, devastated after getting out, bat again.
explanation.walkthrough: An opening pair is a cricket term for the two batsmen who start an innings; here it is just two letters, and gutted means disappointed in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece that was encored was played again because the audience called for more.

clue.text: French city docudrama finally airs

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of docudramA
airs = manners or appearances, miens

explanation.surface: A documentary about a French city is at last broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airs' reads as the verb for broadcasting; it is the noun, meaning bearings or looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a city in northern France, known for its cathedral.

clue.text: Aquatic mammals rolling over, run out and fight

indicators.note: rolling over turns the word the other way up
out in the sense of removed or gone, so the letter for run leaves the word

parts.note: otters are aquatic mammals
R = run, from cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Playful otters tumble over, dash away and scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' looks like the cricket dismissal; here run is R, and out tells you to remove it from SRETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for a short, sharp scrap or quarrel, so it matches fight as a noun.

clue.text: Precise net reduction

parts.note: to net or clear a sum is to make it as profit after costs
a cut is a reduction

explanation.surface: An exact figure for the fall in profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' pulls towards a fishing net or a net figure; the answer uses the verb, as in netting or clearing a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear-cut means precise, sharply defined.

clue.text: For Asians, bread and water after game

parts.note: RU = Rugby Union
pee is a colloquial word for urine, passing water

explanation.surface: Asian cooking, with bread and water served after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, which turns the first part into the definition; the whole of 'bread and water' is not a meal here.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India, Pakistan and other Asian countries, their bread in slang terms.

clue.text: Ignorant landlord interrupts nude dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move around into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
a landlord lets property, so is a letter

explanation.surface: A property owner walks in on a naked dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter is one who lets, the landlord, not a note or character.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlettered means uneducated or unable to read, hence ignorant.

clue.text: Writer's junk mounting

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing upward, so read from the bottom

parts.note: to bin something is to junk it

explanation.surface: An author's rubbish is piling up.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is the pen's nib, the part that does the writing, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: The nib is the writing point of a pen.

clue.text: Section of brig, say, for wife

parts.note: pro = for, in favour of
W = wife

explanation.surface: Part of a naval prison set aside for a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: A brig is a two-masted sailing ship; it is also naval slang for a jail, which is the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The prow is the front section of a ship such as a brig.

clue.text: Accumulated linen garments on appropriate part of anatomy

definitions.meaning: a bottom drawer is linen saved up for married life

definitions.text: garments on appropriate part of anatomy

explanation.surface: Stored-up bedding and underwear, fitted to the right body part.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottom drawer is British for a bride's collection of linen saved for married life; read the other way, drawers (underpants) go on the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottom drawers hold the linen gathered for a future home, and drawers worn on the bottom are underpants.
